name: KKR
coverage: Reviewed KKR India investments across healthcare, consumer businesses and infrastructure. Includes announced transactions, with vehicles and closing uncertainty identified.
limitations: Selective public-disclosure coverage, not a complete portfolio or a live ownership register. The review date does not update the date of an older holding disclosure.
Ownership belongs to the named entity, fund, subsidiary or platform. Fund commitments, acquisitions of assets and joint-venture stakes are not holdings in the listed parent.
Announced investments remain proposed unless closing evidence was reviewed. An unavailable percentage is not zero.
Investment themes and business cases are research interpretations of the cited activity, not forecasts or recommendations.

companies.name: Allfleet India / PMI Electro partnership
companies.relationship: KKR funds agreed a majority investment in Allfleet and a minority investment in PMI Electro.
companies.ownership: Majority in Allfleet / minority in PMI agreed; percentages not disclosed
companies.summary: The announced partnership commits up to US$310 million across the e-bus platform and manufacturer. Closing was not independently established.
companies.thesis: Research interpretation: contracted public transport can create repeatable infrastructure investment opportunities.
companies.risks: Approval, deployment, manufacturing execution and counterparty payment risk.

companies.name: Cisternina Logistics
companies.relationship: KKR-managed funds signed for a majority investment in Cisternina.
companies.ownership: Majority investment agreed; percentage not disclosed
companies.summary: Capital supports the platform, including its proposed acquisition of GBL’s storage-terminal business. This is not a purchase of GBL’s listed shares.
companies.thesis: Research interpretation: storage assets can benefit from trade and industrial supply chains.
companies.risks: Closing conditions, integration, environmental compliance and utilisation.

companies.name: Healthcare Global Enterprises
companies.relationship: Hector Asia Holdings II and KIA EBT II Scheme 1 are named purchasers in the company’s FY26 filing; the earlier agreement covered up to 54%.
companies.ownership: KKR-affiliated acquisition disclosed; current percentage not verified
companies.summary: The named acquisition vehicles provide exposure to HCG. Agreement size is not substituted for a reconciled current holding.
companies.thesis: Research interpretation: specialist hospital networks can expand through clinical capability and operating improvements.
companies.risks: Clinician retention, capital expenditure, clinical outcomes and valuation.

companies.name: Healthium Medtech
companies.relationship: KKR funds announced a controlling acquisition from Apax in 2024; KKR also identifies Healthium in its investment-team material.
companies.ownership: Controlling investment disclosed; current percentage not verified
companies.ownershipDate: 6 May 2024 announcement; team page reviewed 23 Oct 2026
companies.summary: Exposure is through an acquisition vehicle. The reviewed sources do not establish a current retained percentage.
companies.thesis: Research interpretation: surgical consumables offer healthcare-demand and manufacturing exposure.
companies.risks: Product quality, regulation, acquisition leverage and export execution.

companies.name: Serentica Renewables
companies.relationship: KKR names Serentica among its Indian infrastructure investments in its September 2026 release.
companies.summary: Serentica is identified as a decarbonisation platform. No listed-parent stake or ownership percentage is inferred.
companies.thesis: Research interpretation: industrial customers can support long-duration clean-power contracts.
companies.risks: Construction, generation variability, offtaker credit and financing.

companies.name: Vini Cosmetics
companies.relationship: KKR’s India Capstone head identifies Vini among his current board roles.
companies.summary: The official board-role disclosure supports the relationship, without identifying a refreshed ownership percentage.
companies.thesis: Research interpretation: consumer brands can scale through distribution and product execution.
companies.risks: Brand competition, advertising economics and channel execution.

events.title: E-bus partnership signed
events.detail: KKR funds announced a commitment of up to US$310 million across Allfleet and PMI Electro.
events.qualification: A capital commitment and majority/minority description do not establish completed ownership percentages.

events.title: Majority investment agreement for storage platform
events.detail: Funds agreed a majority investment in Cisternina to support expansion and the proposed terminal-business acquisition.
events.qualification: The reviewed source announces definitive agreements, not a verified closing or ownership in listed GBL.

report.title: KKR in India
report.summary: KKR’s disclosed India activity spans business ownership and infrastructure platforms. These six selected relationships include two in-window agreements; percentages remain unavailable where current holdings could not be reconciled.

sections.title: Investment approach
sections.text: KKR’s India outlook spans private equity, infrastructure, climate and credit. This breadth calls for distinguishing company equity from financing and platform-level investments.

sections.title: Healthcare and consumer exposure
sections.text: HCG’s purchaser vehicles, Healthium’s acquisition disclosures and Vini’s board representation are distinct evidence types. Their percentages have not been combined or inferred.

sections.title: Recent agreements
sections.text: The March mobility partnership and September Cisternina agreement are carried as announced transactions. Their contractual scope is retained in the company records.

themes.name: Contracted infrastructure
themes.case: Research interpretation: mobility, storage and renewable platforms suggest interest in assets tied to long-run economic demand.
themes.watch: Closing evidence, contracted returns and financing.

themes.name: Specialist healthcare
themes.case: Research interpretation: hospitals and medical devices offer separate routes to healthcare demand.
themes.watch: Operating outcomes, acquisition execution and valuation.
